title: Towards Training Robustness Against Dynamic Errors in Quantum Machine Learning
problem: Quantum machine learning training assumes static error rates in QNNs, but quantum noise is dynamic across time and qubits, causing performance degradation even when aggregate error rates appear similar.
motivation: NISQ-era quantum machine learning requires robust training strategies that account for dynamic, heterogeneous error conditions across different qubits and time-varying noise profiles.
method: A novel noise-aware training strategy dynamically adjusts to standard and fatal error conditions during QNN optimization, incorporating low-complexity fatal-error detection to identify problematic error patterns and adapt training accordingly.
key_novelty: Dynamic noise-aware training for quantum neural networks that adapts to time-varying and qubit-specific error conditions.
contributions: Novel dynamic NAT strategy addressing time-varying and heterogeneous quantum noise
Low-complexity fatal-error detection method for QNN optimization
Maintains competitive performance with leading NAT methods across varying error scenarios
Improved robustness against dynamic error conditions in NISQ devices

metrics.accuracy: Competitive performance with leading NAT methods across varying error scenarios

limitations: Not discussed; evaluation on simulated quantum noise without real quantum hardware.
primary_theme: Dynamic noise-aware training for quantum neural networks in NISQ era
